newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Megawati supporters defy Indonesia protest warning.
newsitem.headline: Megawati supporters defy Indonesia protest warning.

text.p: Supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri took to the capital's streets on Thursday, ignoring a warning by Indonesian authorities that they would not tolerate further protests by sympathisers of the ousted minority party leader.

About 100 supporters of Megawati marched one km (half a mile) from the office of her chief lawyer to the Central Jakarta State Court to lodge a lawsuit against the man who ousted her as head of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).

The Jakarta Post newspaper on Thursday published comments from armed forces spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi saying that authorities "would not hesitate to take stern action if Megawati loyalists went back onto the streets".

He was speaking after hundreds of Megawati supporters held a six-hour demonstration in front of parliament house in Jakarta on Tuesday, blocking the main thoroughfare alongside and causing huge traffic jams in downtown areas.

Despite the warning, Thursday's march passed off peacefully. Accompanied by a few policemen on motorcycles, the supporters carried banners and chanted "Mega will certainly win" and "Take Surjadi to court" along the way.
Surjadi heads the government-backed PDI faction which ousted Megawati from the party leadership in June last year.

"This is not a demonstration. They have a right to go to court as that is the place for receiving complaints. They are accompanying their lawsuit," Megawati's chief lawyer R.O. Tambunan told Reuters while walking with the group.
The legal action was lodged by 124 Megawati supporters who were arrested and tried after police and members of the government-backed PDI faction raided the party headquarters and took it over.
That action led to the worst rioting in Jakarta in more than two decades. At least five people were killed in the violence and scores of buildings and vehicles were set on fire.

Last November, 115 of the Megawati loyalists arrested were convicted but freed after being sentenced to time served for disobeying police orders. Nine were acquitted. All those convicted have appealed.
"The 124 are suing Surjadi and his colleagues and the head of the Central Jakarta Police for the attack on the PDI headquarters on July 27 which caused them to become victims," Tambunan said.
"They were interned, many were injured and mistreated. They are accusing Surjadi of a political crime and are asking that he pay damages of 100 million rupiah ($41,600) to each of them," he said.
Organisers of Tuesday's demonstration at parliament house said it was a show of support for Megawati ahead of the May 29 general elections.

She has been barred from participating in the polls because her name and those of her supporters were omitted from the list of election candidates supplied by Surjadi's faction, which the government says is the genuine wing of the party.
Indonesia only allows three parties to contest elections -- the PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party -- and election candidates must be approved by the government.
